Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Pramod Kumar Dwivedi 
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
2. Rejoinder affidavit filed today is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Jitendra Kumar Shishodia, Learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Pramod Kumar Dwivedi, learned counsel for opposite party no.2 and Sri Pranshu Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the material available on record.
4.

The present anticipatory bail cancellation application has been filed for cancelling the anticipatory bail granted to opposite party no.2 by this Court vide order dated 6.7.2023 in Anticipatory Bail Application No.6010 of 2023 (Ramjilal Sharma vs. State of U.P. And Another)
arising out of Case Crime No.278 of 2004, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B I.P.C.,
PS- Sadabad, District Hathras.

sentences.text:
1 PROSECUTION STORY:
5. The allegations in the FIR were that opposite party no.2 in collusion with other co-accused persons is stated to have prepared a forged members list of the Management Committee of Sadabad Educational Society for the year 2001-02 and 2002-03 by incorporating the names of several dead persons, as such the applicant and other persons were deprived of their statutory rights for getting elected to the board.
RIVAL CONTENTIONS (Arguments on behalf of applicant)
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that opposite party no.2 has not come with clean hands as he has criminal history of five cases and he has stated in the earlier anticipatory bail application that he had no criminal antecedents to his credit.

The said fact of false statement stands mentioned in paragraph of 5 of the impugned order dated 6.7.2023, as such the order dated 6.7.2023 is liable to be set-aside in light of Section 44 of Indian Evidence Act also.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that the criminal history of five cases are as follows:
"(i) Case Crime No.110/2003, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., Police Station Sadabad, District- Mahamayanagar.
(ii) Case Crime No.89-A/2009, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., Police Station Sadabad, District- Mahamayanagar.
(iii) Case Crime No.0394/2021, under Section 397 I.P.C., Police Station-Sadabad Kotwali, District- Mahamayanagar.

(iv) Case Crime No.144/2002, under Sections 307, 323, 354(b), 452, 504, 506,
3(2)(b) SC/ST Act., Police Station Sadabad, District- Hathras.
(v) Complaint Case No.637/2014, under Sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S.-Sahpau District Hathras".

8. Learned counsel has further stated that of the criminal history of five cases, two cases were instituted prior to the instant FIR i.e. Case Crime Nos.144 of 2002 and 110 of 2003, as such the order dated 06.07.2023 is liable to be set-aside.

entities.text: Case Crime Nos.144 of 2002 and 110 of 2003
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
9. Learned counsel for the applicant has placed much reliance on the judgment of Apex Court passed in S.P. Chengalvaraya Naidu vs. Jagannath1, wherein it has been held as under:
"The principle of "finality of litigation" cannot be pressed to the extent of such an absurdity that it becomes an engine of fraud in the hands of dishonest litigants.
The courts of law are meant for imparting justice between the parties.

One who comes to Mammood Ali Khan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68739187/
2 the court, must come with clean hands.

entities.text: Mammood Ali Khan vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
A person, who's case is based on falsehood,
has no right to approach the court.
He can be summarily thrown out at any stage of the litigation."

10. Learned counsel for the applicant has also placed much reliance on the judgment of Apex Court passed in A.V. Papayya Sastry & Others vs. Government of A.P. & Others2, wherein it has been held as follows:
"It is thus settled proposition of law that a judgment decree or order obtained by playing fraud on the Court Tribunal or Authority is a nullity and not est in the eye of law.

entities.text: A.V. Papayya Sastry & Others vs. Government of A.P. & Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Even the Chief Justice Edward Coke proclaimed 'Fraud avoids all judicial acts'
ecclesiastical or temporal."

(Arguments on behalf of informant/State)
11.

Learned counsel for opposite party no.2 has categorically stated that that instant matter is of the year 2004 and all the cases mentioned in the anticipatory bail cancellation application have been instituted subsequent to the instant FIR, as such they cannot be considered to be the criminal history of opposite party no.2.

12. Learned counsel for opposite party no.2 has further stated that of those five cases, closure report has been filed in one of the cases and in other cases, the investigation is still pending, as such the impugned order cannot be stated to have been procured by making false statement, although he has admitted the fact that there are five cases pending against opposite party no.2.
13.

Learned counsel for opposite party no.2 has also stated that the provision of bail cancellation is not provided in Section 438 Cr.P.C. and the instant bail cancellation application has been filed under Section 439(2) Cr.P.C., which is not maintainable.

CONCLUSION:
14. The clean hands doctrine states that one "who comes into equity must come with clean hands."
This doctrine requires the court to deny equitable relief to a party having violated good faith with respect to the subject of the claim.

The purpose of the doctrine, as elucidated in Colby Furniture Company, Inc. vs. Belinda J. Overton3, is to prevent a party from obtaining relief when that party's own wrongful conduct has made it such that granting the relief would be against equity and good conscience.

entities.text: Colby Furniture Company, Inc. vs. Belinda J. Overton3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. The clean hands doctrine is an affirmative defense that the defendant may claim as has been held in Holy Family Catholic School vs. Boley4, that the plaintiff's abuse of the account necessitated a finding that the plaintiff had "unclean hands" and that requiring the defendant to continue granting relief would be against good conscience.

entities.text: Holy Family Catholic School vs. Boley4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. There are several instances where a person granted bail may have the bail cancelled.

They are:
Mammood Ali Khan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68739187/
3 (i) Where the person during the period of bail, commits the very same offence for which he is being tried or has been convicted, and thereby proves utterly unfit, to be on bail.

entities.text: Mammood Ali Khan vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The parameters on which the bail can be cancelled is covered by condition nos.6 and 7 as the said order is illegal and perverse as it was garnered by suppressing the criminal history of opposite party no.2.
18.
The arguments of counsel for opposite party no.2 that the instant anticipatory bail cancellation application has been filed under Section 439(2) Cr.P.C. does not carry any force.
Thus, the present anticipatory bail cancellation application is allowed.

The order dated 6.7.2023 passed by this Court in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No.6010 of 2023 is hereby set-aside.
19.

However, two weeks' time from the date of pronouncement of this Judgment is granted to opposite party no.2 to surrender before the concerned Trial Court and thereafter it will be open for opposite party no. 2 to pray for regular bail, which may be considered in accordance with law laid down by the Apex Court in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another5,
2022 SCC OnLine SC 825.
Order Date :- 15.2.2024
